violations.title: Before Use After Cleaning
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment were not observed sanitized: - OBSERVED: the sanitizing step of chemical dishwasher (left unit) was not verified. Observed a sanitizing rinse concentration less than 50ppm chlorine solution.
violations.corrective_action: All utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use and after cleaning. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: service engineer came down and repaired the dishwasher immediately.

violations.title: Cooling from Ambient to 41F, No More than 4 Hours
violations.observation: The following food item prepared from ambient air temperature ingredients is not being adequately cooled to 41F or less within 4 hours: (1) salmon (42-43f) and spring mix (42-43f) were stored in 3-door flat top cooler for 4 hours; (2) noodles (55f) were stored in 3-door flat top cooler for 3 hours and then relocated to ice bath for 1 hour; (3) cut cantaloupe (42-43f) and tofu (42f) were stored in true 3-door upright cooler overnight.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 4 hours to 41F or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient air temperature (i.e. reconstituted foods and canned tuna). - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: CFM discarded the food items.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: - OBSERVED: (1) salmon skin (62f) was stored on the drain board of 3-compartment sink for 30 minutes. (2) diced tofu (55f) and seaweed (56f) were stored on ice bath for 3 hours
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: (1) CFM relocated the salmon skin on ice bath; (2) food items will be discarded within 1 hour.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: - OBSERVED: sushi rice stored in two sushi makers was not marked with start and end time.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to-eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: EHS discussed TPHC with CFM and instructed CFM to label the sushi rice with start and end time.

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: - OBSERVED: frozen tuna was thawing in intact reduced oxygen packaging.
violations.corrective_action: - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: EHS educated CFM on thawing methods for ROP fish and instructed CFM to make a cut in each ROP.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: - OBSERVED: squeeze bottles of pesto sauce, strawberry sauce, and mango sauce were not properly labeled.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: EHS instructed CFM to label all squeeze bottles properly.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. A FOOD EMPLOYEE DIDN’T WASH HANDS AFTER CRACKING EGGS AND BEFORE PREPARING FOOD.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. CFM EDUCATED THE FOOD EMPLOYEE. WASABI (Inspection Date: 09/03/2025) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: A UTENSIL WAS STORED IN A CONTAINER OF STAGNANT WATER AT 98F.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. CFM REMOVED THE WATER.

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: Reduced Oxygen Packaged Tuna observed thawing in 2 door prep refrigerator inside of sealed vacuum packaging.
violations.corrective_action: Reduced Oxygen Packaging (ROP) removes oxygen from the package and may allow growth of anaerobic microbes at refrigeration temperatures. Follow all manufacturer instructions for thawing. Person-In-Charge cut the corner of each bag that was thawing to allow for air to enter the packaging.
